`planted-gotcha.md` describes one gotcha, reported below as one finding. No files were changed.

The gotcha is that `.slice()` on a Node.js `Buffer` returns a view, a second handle onto the same memory, so a write through the slice also changes the original buffer. The file names no fix, so the resolution in the finding (copy with `Buffer.from(buf)` when independent bytes are needed) comes from general Node.js knowledge and was not run here.

```rafa:report
status: done
feedback: |
  Read planted-gotcha.md and reported the gotcha it describes as one finding. The file states the behaviour only; the resolution field is general Node.js knowledge and was not executed in this session. No files were changed and no commands were run beyond reading the file.
findings:
  - trigger: "when calling .slice() on a Node.js Buffer and then writing through the result"
    kind: gotcha
    what: "Buffer.slice() returns a view onto the same underlying memory, so writing through the slice also mutates the bytes of the buffer it was sliced from"
    cause: "a Buffer slice shares the original buffer's memory instead of copying it, unlike Array.prototype.slice"
    resolution: "copy explicitly when independent bytes are needed, for example Buffer.from(buf) or Uint8Array.prototype.slice.call(buf), and treat a slice as a shared view"
    artifact: ".slice()"
    signal: silent
    domain: general-best-practices
skills_used: []

changes:
  - level: none
    summary: "no code changed; the planted gotcha was read and reported as a finding"
```
